Answer: C
Reason: Dysphonia (hoarseness) is a classic symptom of recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy, which can be caused by compression from enlarged mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes. The left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops under the aortic arch near the left hilum, making enlargement of the left hilum (Option C) the most likely finding to correlate with this symptom in the context of a malignancy like tracheal squamous cell carcinoma.
